description.en:
Adds a pinball-style bumper to the match pitch, in one call. Unlike tornadoes and flippers, a bumper needs no second call and no handle is returned.

Two things are created:
- a collision body built from the full 3D position and the five shape values (the engine registers it as kind 4);
- an entry of kind 1 in the pitch-object table, placed at the position's X and Z.

The five values are named h, w, c, min and max in the shipped script (30, 20, 1.1, 80 and 120). Their exact roles were not traced; a c above 1 and a min/max pair would fit a bounce factor with a speed range, which is what a pinball bumper does, but that reading is not confirmed.
3-element array [x, y, z]. The collision body uses all three; the pitch-object entry uses x and z.
First shape value (h in the shipped script, 30.0).
Second shape value (w in the shipped script, 20.0).

Third shape value (c in the shipped script, 1.1).
The native only checks that 3 arguments are present, but it always reads all six, so pass them all.
Fourth shape value (min in the shipped script, 80.0).
Fifth shape value (max in the shipped script, 120.0).

true once the bumper is added.
null if the match system is not ready or fewer than 3 arguments were given.

examples.case: The four corner bumpers of the pinball pitch (real usage, from mf14b01.nut)
